newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL interbank rates steady as bidding increases.
newsitem.headline: KL interbank rates steady as bidding increases.

text.p: Interbank rates were steady to slightly higher on increased bidding by local banks covering their positions, dealers said on Monday.
They said the domestic financial institutions were expecting the shortage of liquidity to continue in the near-term.
"Realising that this situation (of tightness) is not likely to go away very soon, the local banks are covering their positions," said a senior dealer at a Malaysian bank.
He said there were larger number of borrowers in the market on Monday.
This pushed up the one-week interbank rate to 11/13 percent against 10/11 percent on Friday and two-week was steady at 9.0/11 percent.
One-month money at 8.5/9.0 percent and three-month and six-month at 7.5/9.0 percent, were trading unchanged.
The dealers said the overnight interbank rate, which closed at its recent high of 18/20 percent on Friday, was expected to remain unchanged.

The rise in interbank rates started 10 days ago, after Bank Negara intervened aggressively in the foreign exchange market to stem the slide of the ringgit. The central bank was said to have sold around $1 billion worth of dollars.
The intervention drained liquidity from the system, causing the market to be short and interbank rates to rise to unusually high levels.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange were lower across the board, reflecting the sentiment in the cash market, futures dealers said.
The three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) contract for June 1997 was down seven points at 92.44, or an implied yield of 7.56 percent.
September 1997 contract was down four at 92.56, or 7.54 percent and December was steady at 92.57, or 7.43 percent.
